questions.prompt: What is a group on the periodic table?
questions.explanation: A group is a vertical column — elements stacked one above another share the same group and similar behavior.
questions.misconception: Rows and columns are easy to swap — the horizontal rows are called periods, and the vertical columns are the groups.

questions.prompt: What do all the elements in one group share?
options: The same number of valence electrons
questions.explanation: Elements in a group share the same number of valence electrons — the electrons in the outermost shell — which is what makes them behave alike.
questions.misconception: Shell count (which changes down a column) and atomic mass are shared by rows or not at all — the shared trait within a column is valence electrons.

questions.prompt: Why are elements in the same group chemically similar?
options: Same valence electrons means similar bonding and reactivity
They all have the same mass
questions.explanation: Because valence electrons control how atoms bond and react, sharing that count means sharing similar chemical behavior.
questions.misconception: Physical looks and state of matter vary within a group — it is the electron arrangement, not appearance, that drives the chemical similarity.

questions.prompt: Group 18 is the noble gases. What do they all share?
options: Full outer shells, making them very unreactive
One valence electron, making them very reactive
questions.explanation: Noble gases all have full outer shells, so they have no need to gain, lose, or share electrons — which makes them famously unreactive.
questions.misconception: It's the alkali metals (Group 1) with one valence electron that are famously reactive — full shells, not empty ones, are what make the noble gases so stable.
